Re your question on VARA HF bandwidth. On the free version you're capped at the 500 Hz mode speed anyway so dont bother with the 2300 setting unless you buy the license. I'm running 2750 on mine, getting SL 10-12 to the gateway in Kansas most evenings on 40m.

Caught a mahi on day 8, ate it for 3 days. Anna is reading her way through every book on board. I'm fixing things, as usual. Today it was the autopilot linkage, a cotter pin had walked out. Easy fix.

Love to all,
Sam and Anna

Re: VARA settings

You need to set the TCP ports the same in VARA and Winlink Express. Default is 8300 command and 8301 data. If you changed one you have to change both. That's 90% of the 'VARA not connecting' questions I get.

To the board:

I've been thinking about the repeater controller replacement we talked about. Options I see:

A. Repair the old one. The guy in Tulsa says $180 plus shipping, 3-4 week turnaround. It's 22 years old, something else will die next.

B. Buy a new Arcom or similar, about $650 with the voice board. Plug and play mostly, I'd need a weekend to program it.

C. Build something from a Raspberry Pi with an off-the-shelf interface. Cheap ($150ish) but its a hobby project, and if it breaks at 2am during a storm net nobody will know how to fix it except me.

I lean to B. We have $1,900 in the repeater fund. I'll put it on the agenda for the 18th unless anyone objects strongly.

Your question about the 30m dipole. Formula is 468/f so for 10.130 MHz you get about 46.2 ft total, 23.1 per leg. Cut it a bit long, like 24 ft per leg, and trim. Each inch makes about 30 kHz difference at that freq, roughly.

Hey Joe,

Thanks for asking about the trip. It went great. We spent 2 weeks in the Boundary Waters, entry point 25 out of Ely. Paddled about 80 miles total. Saw loons, beaver, a wolf (!), and way too many mosquitoes.

Radio-wise I brought the KX2 and a 41 ft wire with a 9:1 unun, a small 3Ah LiFePO4 and a folding 20W panel. Sent a winlink check-in every evening to my wife through the gateway in Minneapolis. Only failed twice, both nights during a thunderstorm when I didn't want to put up the antenna anyway.

The hardest part was keeping everything dry. Next time I'm bringing a better dry bag for the radio, the cheap one leaked.

Grids if you want them: EN47 and EN57 mostly.

73
